task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

historical_evidence.finding: Split-half reliability of Connector teammate-path quality Q_p was low (r=0.215, Spearman-Brown 0.355, ICC 0.216), indicating that most variance is within-player half-to-half and the measure is too unreliable to treat Q_p as a stable scoutable trait.

Validation of ranked playsheet based on H1-to-H2 PPP drops found weak full-rank signal (Spearman rho=-0.0639), but pairwise BEST vs AVOID comparison showed a significant effect; identified risks: leakage, low measurement reliability, small sample, drift.
Initial positive lag-1 PPP effect after star foul was largely driven by free throws (artifact); after excluding free throws the effect disappeared.
PCI's incremental R2 over ORtg was mainly due to leakage tracking DRtg; the offensive-control component added only 0.005 R2, revealing an artifact from construction.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Split-half reliability test for a derived player-level metric (Connector Q_p)
failed_approaches.why: Low measurement reliability (MEASURE_RELIABILITY), leading to untestable conclusion due to high within-player half-to-half variance.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranked playsheet prediction using H1-to-H2 PPP changes
failed_approaches.why: Inconclusive due to small sample, measurement noise, and leakage/confounding; Spearman rank correlation not significantly positive.
Initial positive result was artifact from free throws; after proper control, no significant effect; risks included BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, MECHANICAL_FLOOR.
Apparent incremental R2 was leakage tracking DRtg; artifact from construction.

evidence_establishes: Derived half-to-half metrics can suffer from low measurement reliability at the player level (SF-[prior work]).
Half-to-half PPP changes are susceptible to artifacts (e.g., free throw spikes) and confounds that can mimic or obscure real effects ([prior work], SF-[prior work]).
Small sample sizes and measurement noise often lead to inconclusive results for advanced on-off metrics (SF-[prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a defense's effect on opponent H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait has not been directly tested.
The degree of year-to-year stability of any such team-level metric remains unknown.
The specific sample size and power needed to detect a team-level defensive H2-H1 trait in NBA data have not been determined.
own_inferences: Given the noise in single-game half-to-half PPP differences, aggregating to a season-level metric still requires many games to overcome measurement error; with only 120 team-seasons, year-to-year reliability tests will be underpowered unless the true signal is very strong.
Confounding by game script (score margin, end-of-quarter tactics, lineup changes, garbage time) can induce team-level patterns in H2-H1 change that may be mistaken for a defensive trait.
The low reliability of a conceptually similar player-level half-to-half metric warns that attenuation is likely for this team-level measure, making it difficult to establish a stable trait.
uncertainties: The true inter-team variance in defensive H2-H1 suppression is unknown; it could be large enough to overcome expected measurement noise.
The reliability of the metric over a full 82-game season may be higher than player-level half-to-half reliability, but the magnitude is not yet estimated.
Novel adjustments for opponent strength and game script could reduce confounds, but their effectiveness and validity remain uncertain without pilot testing.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieval returned records showing that similarly motivated half-to-half derived metrics exhibited low measurement reliability and were often untestable or artifact-ridden. This evidence shifted the assessment toward a high risk of untestability and led to a recommendation not to proceed, whereas without it one might have assumed a simple reliability design could work.

blocking_constraints.text: Half-to-half change in opponent points per possession is a noisy metric per game; aggregating over a season may still yield low reliability if underlying trait effect is small, as historical player-level evidence suggests.
Only 120 team-seasons across 4 seasons; a year-to-year correlation test would have about 90 paired observations, giving low power to detect a weak reliability (e.g., ICC<0.25).
Game script (score margin, end-of-quarter strategies, garbage time) affects second-half possession quality, potentially creating spurious defensive signals that are not a stable team trait.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved study directly tested the reliability of a team-level defensive opponent H2-H1 change trait. Indirect evidence from player-level half-to-half metrics and artifact-prone PPP change studies provides context but does not answer the question.

risks.text: Single-game H2-H1 PPP differences have high variance; a full-season average may still be unreliable if underlying signal is weak.
120 team-seasons and ~90 paired year-to-year observations provide insufficient power to detect a small-to-moderate reliability coefficient.
Game script confounds (score differential at half, opponent tactics, rotations) are difficult to fully adjust and may persist as spurious team effects.
If teams are selected by extreme H2-H1 values, regression to the mean may create illusory instability across seasons.
If the true between-team variance in H2-H1 suppression is near zero, the metric will inherently be unreliable.
Testing multiple operationalizations or slice-and-dice subgroups without correction inflates the false positive rate.
Rule changes, playing style trends, and season-specific fatigue/scheduling could alter the defensive trait across seasons, undermining year-to-year stability.

design.estimand: Season-level Spearman-Brown corrected reliability of a team's average opponent second-half minus first-half points per possession (PPP), adjusted for pre-game opponent offensive rating and in-game score differential at half.
design.sample: All 120 team-seasons from 2022-23 through 2025-26. For split‑half reliability, each team's games within a season are randomly partitioned into two halves (balanced on home/away and opponent strength). For year‑to‑year stability, pair consecutive seasons for the same team (max 90 pairs).
design.power: Split‑half: if true full-season ICC=0.2, half-season Spearman-Brown-corrected estimate would require ~400 team-seasons for 80% power, far exceeding available data. Year‑over‑year correlation: 90 pairs can detect r=0.29 at 80% power, but a weak trait (r<0.2) would be undetectable.
design.controls: Adjust opponent H2-H1 PPP by subtracting the same opponent's average H2-H1 PPP in all non-garbage games (or use a mixed model). Include a non‑linear function of half-time score margin (e.g., restricted cubic spline) to account for game script. Exclude possessions classified as garbage time (last 5 minutes, 20+ point margin).
design.falsification: Test whether the team's own H2-H1 offensive PPP change shows similar reliability; a genuine defensive trait should not symmetrically appear on offense. Placebo test: randomly shuffle opponent assignments to break defensive pairings and confirm zero reliability.
design.multiplicity: Pre‑register a single primary metric: Spearman-Brown corrected split‑half reliability of adjusted opponent H2-H1 PPP change. No unplanned subgroup analyses; if explored, apply Holm-Bonferroni correction.
design.decision_rule: Conclude the trait is reliable if the corrected reliability coefficient exceeds 0.5 and its 95% CI lower bound exceeds 0.3. If the raw split-half correlation is <0.2, declare the test underpowered and interpret results as inconclusive.
design.data_version: NBA stats API play-by-play data as of 2026-10-06, processed into half-level PPP using derived play‑type possession records.
